chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-K Muhammad al-Kinji from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban ibn Uthman from Abdullah ibn Muhraz who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to me and died, and left a daughter. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Give the daughter half, and leave for the guardians half.'

So I returned. So our companions said, 'No, by Allah, there is nothing for the guardians.' So I returned to him the next day and said to him, 'Our companions said, there is nothing for the guardians, and it was out of dissimulation for you.' So he said, 'No, by Allah, I was not dissimulative to you, but I feared over you that you would be seized for the half. So if you are not afraid, hand over the other half to the daughter, for Allah will be Leading you.'

key_terms.اتَّقَاكَ: It was out of dissimulation/precaution for you
key_terms.الْمَوَالِي: Guardians or close relatives (often used for the deceased's clan or freedmen in inheritance contexts)
key_terms.تُؤْخَذَ بِالنِّصْفِ: You would be seized/required to pay the half

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on inheritance when a man leaves a daughter and bequeaths to a non-heir, according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the nuanced application of *taqiyyah* (precautionary dissimulation) in inheritance law, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) initially attributed a half-share to the *mawali* (freedmen/clients) to protect the heir from potential liability, rather than stating the definitive legal ruling. It highlights the distinction between the juristic consensus that *mawali* receive no share in the absence of other heirs and the practical wisdom of the Imam in safeguarding the bequeather. The narrative underscores the Imam's authority to adjust rulings based on the specific fears and circumstances of the questioner.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Al Kindy, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdullah Bin Muhraz who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who bequeathed to me and died, and left a daughter. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Give the daughter, the half, and leave for the guardians, the half’.

So I returned. So our companions said, ‘No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, there is nothing for the guardians’. So I returned to meet him<sup>asws</sup>, so I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Our companions said, ‘There is nothing for the guardians, but rather it was out of dissimulation for you’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I<sup>asws</sup> was not dissimulative to you, but I feared over you that you would be seized for the half. So if you are not afraid, so hand over the other half to the daughter, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will be Leading you’.
en.sarwar: 9. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad al-Kindiy from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Mithamiy from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhriz who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who made a will to me and died, leaving behind his daughter. He (the Imam) said, ‘Give one-half to his daughter and leave the other half for al-Mawali (friends, guardians or masters).’
I then returned to our people and they said, ‘No, by Allah, there is nothing for al-Mawali.’

I went back to him (the Imam) and informed him that our people say, ‘There is nothing for al-Mawali. He (the Imam) has said so because of fear (taqiyah).’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, by Allah, I did not do so because of fear ( taqiyah ) but I was afraid for you that you will be asked about one-half. If you are not afraid; give the other half also to his daughter and Allah will relieve you of the burden.’”
